"Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng First"
"Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng killed Chén Xià Zhēngshū,
the *Chūnqiū* devalued the writing about it,
not granting it a special discussion;
Líng Wáng killed Qí Qìngfēng,
and directly called him 'Chǔ Zǐ',
why?"
He said:
"Zhuāng Wáng's actions were virtuous,
and Zhēngshū's crimes were serious.
When a virtuous ruler punishes a serious crime,
it is good in the eyes of the people.
If it were not devalued,
who would know that it was not orthodox?
The *Chūnqiū* always uses cases where one seems to be gaining something improperly
to show their lack of propriety.
Therefore, Qí Huán was not granted a special territory to enfeoff,
Jìn Wén was not granted the authority to bring a king to audience and court,
Chǔ Zhuāng was not granted the authority to specially kill and punish.
If these three were not allowed,
then the attainments of the feudal lords,
would almost be diminished!
This is why Chǔ Líng was called 'Zǐ' when he carried out the punishment.
The language of the *Chūnqiū* is often allegorical,
its writing is concise, but its rules are clear."
Someone asked:
"The fact that the feudal lords were not allowed to make exclusive enfeoffments is
demonstrated again by the destruction of Chén and Cài.
The fact that the feudal lords were not allowed to make exclusive punitive expeditions,
why is this not demonstrated again by the killing by Qìng Fēng?
Why is that?"
He replied:
"The use of language in the *Spring and Autumn Annals* is such that
what is already clear is omitted,
and what is not clear is recorded.
Now, the fact that the feudal lords are not allowed to make exclusive punitive expeditions
is already clear.
However, Qìng Fēng's crime has not been shown,
therefore, it refers to the Viscount of Chǔ using his hegemonic position to punish him,
recording that his crime deserved death,
to establish a great prohibition for the world.
It says:
the actions of a subject,
which degrade the position of the lord,
and the ministers who cause chaos in the state,
even if they do not usurp and kill,
their crimes all deserve death.
Compared to this,
that is the reason."
"The *Spring and Autumn Annals* says:
'Jìn attacked Xiān Yú.'
Why does it consider Jìn evil and equate it with the barbarian Di tribes?"
Said:
"The *Chūnqiū* (
Trust is valued more than land,
and ritual is honored more than one's own person.
How do we know this is so?
Sòng Bójī (宋伯姬) feared impropriety and died in the fire;
Qí Huángōng (齊桓公) suspected trust and diminished his land.
The *Chūnqiū* deemed them virtuous and recorded them,
as models for the world.
To speak of ritual and trust,
no ritual will go unanswered,
and no act of generosity will go unreturned;
this is the way of Heaven.
Now my ruler and minister, being of the same surname, marry off a daughter.
The daughter has no conscience,
so the ritual receives no response.
There is fear that they might fear me;
how is this not barbarian-like!
During the rebellion of Gōngzǐ Qìngfù (公子慶父),
Lǔ (魯) was in grave danger of annihilation,
yet Qí Huángōng (齊桓公) secured it.
He had no familial connection to them,
yet he still came to worry about us.
How can you, being of the same surname, treat us with such cruelty and violence?
The *Shī* (*Classic of Poetry*, 詩) says:
'Look at that cooing dove,
its wings flying up to Heaven.
My heart is saddened,
Thinking of those ancestors.
At daybreak I cannot sleep,
my heart cherishes those two men."
All men have this feeling.
Now Jìn is not worried about me because we share the same surname,
but because it is strong, it is repulsed by me,
and my heart is disappointed.
Therefore, when the words are not good,
saying only "It's Jìn,"
is a euphemism."
The questioner said:
"Jìn is wicked and cannot be approached,
you went but dared not arrive,
this is only human nature.
Why would a *jūnzǐ* be ashamed and claim to be ill?"
He replied:
"Evil comes without reason,
a *jūnzǐ* is not ashamed.
Introspecting and finding no fault,
what worry, what fear?
That is all.
Now, the *Chūnqiū* shames those [who are ashamed],
*Zhāo Gōng* had reason to incur it.
Ministers overstep their rulers,
beginning with *Wén* and becoming extreme with *Zhāo*.
The duke received a chaotic decline,
and had no heart of fear or alertness,
Acting rashly and lightly planning reckless attacks,
violating great propriety by marrying someone of the same surname,
and embracing injustice while heavily degrading oneself.
People say:
"When a state is well-governed,
the neighboring states congratulate it;
when a state is in turmoil,
the neighboring states scatter."
Therefore, Jì Sūn monopolized his position,
and the major states did not rectify him.
He fled for eight years,
and only after his death was he allowed to return.
He himself perished and his son was endangered,
the height of misfortune.
A gentleman is not ashamed of his hardship,
but is ashamed of the reason for his impoverishment.
Although Zhāo Gōng encountered this time,
if he had not married someone of the same surname,
how could he have reached this point?
Even if he had married someone of the same surname,
if he had been able to employ Kǒngzǐ to assist him,
he would also not have reached this point.
The times were difficult but governance was simple,
and he acted perversely without rescue;
this is the reason for his impoverishment."
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* divides twelve generations into three categories:
those witnessed,
There are those seen,
there are those heard about.
Those seen, span three generations;
those heard about, four generations;
those passed down by hearsay, five generations.
Therefore, (the events during the reigns of) Duke Āi, Duke Dìng, Duke Zhāo,
are what the gentleman personally witnessed.
(The events during the reigns of) Duke Xiāng, Duke Chéng, Duke Wén, Duke Xuān,
are what the gentleman heard about.
(The events during the reigns of) Duke Xī, Duke Mǐn, Duke Zhuāng, Duke Huán, Duke Yǐn,
are what the gentleman learned of through hearsay.
Those seen, cover sixty-one years;
those heard about, eighty-five years;
those learned by hearsay, ninety-six years.
Regarding those seen,
the words are subtle;
regarding those heard about,
the calamities are lamented;
regarding those learned by hearsay,
the favors are suppressed;
all accord with feelings.
Therefore, in expelling the Jì clan and speaking of holding another *yú* sacrifice,
the words are subtle.
Zǐ Chì was killed,
(and) it could not be borne to record the day,
the calamities are lamented.
Zǐ Bān was killed,
and recorded as *yǐ wèi*,
It eliminates the kindness toward them.
The intention to yield and stretch,
the detailed and concise writing,
all respond to it.
I believe that it treats those near as near and those far as far, those who are close as close and those who are distant as distant,
and also understands that it values the valued and despises the despised, weighs the heavy and light,
and also understands that it treats the generous as generous and the stingy as stingy, the good as good and the evil as evil,
and also understands that it treats the bright as bright and the dark as dark, the white as white and the black as black.
All things have pairs,
pair them and unite them,
match the enemies and pair them,
good!
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Dignified and restrained,
virtuous words orderly,
without resentment or wickedness,
following the ranks of peers."
This is what it means.
Therefore, the *Spring and Autumn Annals* is the greatest of righteousness;
grasp one end and understand it broadly;
observe its right and wrong,
and you can obtain its correct method;
observe its gentle words,
and you can know how to stop resentment.
Therefore, externally,
it speaks of the Way but does not make it obvious;
internally,
it conceals but does not hide completely;
It is the same with respect for superiors;
It is the same with respect for the worthy;
This is how one distinguishes between inner and outer, differentiates between the worthy and the unworthy, and equalizes the honored and the humble.
Righteousness does not slander superiors,
Wisdom does not endanger oneself,
Therefore, those far away conceal through righteousness,
Those nearby are awed by wisdom,
When awe and righteousness are combined,
then as the generation gets closer, speech becomes more cautious.
This is why the words of Duke Dìng and Duke Āi were subtle.
Therefore, if it is applied, the world is at peace;
if it is not applied, one secures one's own person;
this is the Dao of the *Spring and Autumn Annals*.
The Dao of the *Spring and Autumn Annals*
Reveres Heaven and models itself on antiquity.
Therefore, even with skillful hands,
if one does not follow the compass and square,
one cannot correct squares and circles;
even with discerning ears,
if one does not play the six pitch-pipes,
one cannot determine the five tones;
even with a wise heart,
if one does not examine the former kings,
one cannot bring peace to the world.
Then, the way left behind by the former kings,
is indeed the compass, square, and pitch-pipes of the world!
Therefore, the sages model themselves on Heaven,
The wise emulate the sages,
this is the great principle;
obtain the great principle and there is order,
lose the great principle and there is chaos,
this is the distinction between order and chaos;
it is said that under Heaven there are not two paths,
therefore the sages have different governance but the same principle,
they are thoroughly versed in the past and present,
therefore the former sages transmitted their methods to later generations.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals*'s relationship to world affairs
is that it excels at restoring the ancient ways,
and it censures changing the norm,
desiring to emulate the methods of the former kings.
However, it is introduced with one statement, saying:
"A king must change institutions."
The self-willed obtain this as an excuse,
saying:
"If the past could be followed,
why did the ways of the former kings not continue to follow one another?"
The world is confused by hearing this,
and doubts the correct path while believing in heretical words,
which is deeply concerning.
I answer them, saying:
"There was a man who heard that the lords of the feudal states enjoyed the music of 'Shooting the Leopard Head,'
so he cut off a leopard's head himself,
hung it up and shot at it,
saying:
'Where is the enjoyment in this?'
This is hearing the name without knowing the reality.
What is now called the new king necessarily changing the system,
is not changing the Way,
is not altering the principle.
Receiving the Mandate from Heaven,
changing the surname and replacing the king,
is not succeeding the former king to rule.
If one merely follows the previous system,
cultivates the old affairs,
and has nothing changed,
then there is no way to distinguish it from succeeding the former king to rule.
The ruler who receives the Mandate,
is what Heaven greatly reveals.
Serving a father is to inherit his intentions,
serving a ruler is to model his will,
serving Heaven is also the same.
Now, if Heaven greatly reveals itself,
and things inherit what has been replaced and generally remain the same,
then it is neither revealing nor clear,
and is not the will of Heaven.
Therefore, one must move residences, change titles, reform the calendar, and change clothing colors;
there is no other reason,
than daring not to disobey the will of Heaven and to clearly reveal oneself.
If the great principles, human relationships, doctrines, politics, teachings, customs, and literary meanings are all as before,
then what is there to change?
Therefore, a king has the name of changing the system,
but not the reality of changing the Way.
Kǒngzǐ (Confucius) said:
"He who governs by non-action,
is it not Shùn!"
This speaks only of the way of his lord Yáo,
is this not the effect of no change!"
The questioner said:
"Things change and Heaven bestows,
it is clear,
but why must new music be made?"
What is the reason?"
He replied:
"Music is different from this.
Institutions are made in response to heavenly changes,
music is made in response to human changes.
Those who receive the mandate
must share joy with the people.
Therefore, great changes in institutions are made at the beginning,
to clarify the mandate of Heaven;
the making of new music is done at the end,
to display the accomplishment of Heaven;
based on what the world newly delights in, one creates musical compositions,
to harmonize the government
and to promote virtue,
before the world is universally in harmony,
the ruler does not make music in vain.
Music is that which is full within and moves and emanates outwards,
responding to the time of governance,
establishing rites and making music to complete it,
completion means that the fundamental, the subsidiary, the substance, and the ornamentation are all complete.
Therefore, those who create music must always look back to what the world initially found pleasing, taking their own pleasure as the foundation.
In the time of Shùn,
the people rejoiced in his making Yáo's achievements manifest,
hence the music called "Sháo."
"Sháo" means to manifest;
in the time of Yǔ,
the people rejoiced that three sages succeeded one another,
hence the music called "Xià."
"Xià" means great;
in the time of Tāng,
the people rejoiced that he rescued them from calamity and harm,
hence the music called "Hù."
"Hù" means rescue;
in the time of King Wén,
the people rejoiced in his raising armies and launching conquests,
hence the music called "Wǔ."
"Wǔ" means conquest.
These four were universally enjoyed throughout the world,
and were one and the same
but the reasons for this common joy
are not the same.
The method of creating music
must always revert to the source of what is pleasurable.
If what is pleasurable is not the same in each event,
how could the music not change from generation to generation!
Therefore, Shùn created "Sháo," and Yǔ created "Xià,"
Tāng created "Hù," and King Wén created "Wǔ."
These four pieces of music have different names
then each would obey his people, and begin to find joy in himself.
I have seen its effects.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"King Wén received the mandate,
and possessed such martial accomplishments;
having attacked Chóng,
he built the city of Fēng."
This is the style of *lè* (music).
It also says:
"The King was greatly angered,
and then mustered his troops."
At that time,
Zhòu was without the proper Way,
the feudal lords were in great disarray,
and the people rejoiced at the anger of King Wén and sang of it.
The virtue of the people of Zhōu had already reached all under heaven,
they returned to the root as their joy,
and called it "The Great Martial (Dà Wǔ),"
saying that what the people initially rejoiced in was martial prowess, that is all.
Therefore, generally, with all music,
it is created at the end,
but named by its beginning,
emphasizing the meaning of the root.
Viewed from this,
changes in the calendar and official clothing,
the differences in receiving the mandate, responding to heaven, establishing rites, and creating music,
are all movements of the human heart,
these two separate but then reunite,
What is done is the same."
"Jade Cup, Number Two"
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* criticized Duke Wén for marrying during the mourning period.
The challenger said:
"The rules of mourning,
do not exceed three years;
the three years of mourning,
is twenty-five months.
Now, according to the *Classic*,
Duke Wén married after forty-one months,
when he married, there was no mourning.
It had long been outside the rules;
why call it marrying during mourning?"
He replied:
"'The Spring and Autumn Annals' in discussing matters,
places the greatest importance on intention.
Now, marriage inevitably involves offering betrothal gifts,
and the month of offering betrothal gifts fell within the mourning period.
Therefore, it is called marrying during mourning.
Furthermore, Duke Wén performed the autumn *xiá* sacrifice
and offered betrothal gifts in winter.
Both were excessively early.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* does not criticize what came before,
but only criticizes what came after.
Certainly, the three years of mourning,
is a matter of heartfelt emotion.
Even if one follows custom and cannot complete it,
猶宜未平於心， [yóu yí wèi píng yú xīn,] It would still be appropriate for his heart not to be at peace.
今全無悼遠之志， [jīn quán wú dào yuǎn zhī zhì,] But now he has no intention of mourning the deceased at all.
反思念娶事， [fǎn sīniàn qǔ shì,] On the contrary, he is thinking about the matter of taking a wife.
是《春秋》之所甚疾也， [shì "chūn qiū" zhī suǒ shèn jí yě,] This is what the *Spring and Autumn Annals* severely condemns.
故譏不出三年於首而已， [gù jī bù chū sān nián yú shǒu ér yǐ,] Therefore, it criticizes that he does not complete even the three years of mourning,
譏以喪娶也。 [jī yǐ sàng qǔ yě.] Criticizing him for marrying during mourning.
不別先後， [bù bié xiān hòu,] Not distinguishing between what should come first and what should come after,
賤其無人心也。 [jiàn qí wú rén xīn yě.] Devalues him for having no human feelings.
緣此以論禮， [yuán cǐ yǐ lùn lǐ,] Based on this to discuss ritual,
禮之所重者在其志， [lǐ zhī suǒ zhòng zhě zài qí zhì,] what ritual values is in one's intentions.
志敬而節具， [zhì jìng ér jié jù,] If one's intentions are reverent and the formalities are complete,
則君子予之知禮； [zé jūnzǐ yǔ zhī zhī lǐ;] then the gentleman will acknowledge that he understands ritual.
志和而音雅， [zhì hé ér yīn yǎ,] If one's intentions are harmonious and the music is refined,
則君子予之知樂； [zé jūnzǐ yǔ zhī zhī yuè;] then the gentleman will acknowledge that he understands music.
志哀而居約， [zhì āi ér jū yuē,] If one's intentions are mournful and one lives frugally,
則君子予之知喪。 [zé jūnzǐ yǔ zhī zhī sàng.] then the gentleman will acknowledge that he understands mourning.
故曰： [gù yuē:] Therefore it is said:
非虛加之， [fēi xū jiā zhī,] Not to add them emptily,
重志之謂也。 [zhòng zhì zhī wèi yě.] It is to value intentions.
志為質， [zhì wèi zhì,] Intention is the substance,
物為文， [wù wèi wén,] the outward forms are the ornamentation.
文著於質， [wén zhù yú zhì,] The ornamentation is manifested in the substance,
質不居文， [zhì bù jū wén,] If the substance does not dwell in the ornamentation,
文安施質； [wén ān shī zhì;] where shall the ornamentation be applied?
質文兩備， [zhì wén liǎng bèi,] When both substance and ornamentation are complete,
然後其禮成； [ránhòu qí lǐ chéng;] then the ritual is complete.
文質偏行， [wén zhì piān xíng,] If either ornamentation or substance is pursued alone,
不得有我爾之名； [bùdé yǒu wǒ ěr zhī míng;] neither you nor I will gain a good reputation.
When both cannot be fully achieved and one is prioritized,
it is better to have substance without embellishment.
Even if it doesn't quite reach the standard of propriety,
it is still somewhat virtuous.
The arrival of Jiè Gélú 介葛盧 is an example of this.
To have embellishment without substance
is not only not acceptable,
but even somewhat detestable.
The arrival of Zhōu Gōng Shí 州公寔 is an example of this.
Therefore, the order of priorities in the *Chūnqiū* 春秋 is to
value substance first and embellishment after,
prioritize intention on the right and material things on the left.
Therefore, it is said:
"Ritual, ritual!
Is it merely about jade and silk?"
Extend this forward,
and one should also say:
"Court audience, court audience!
Is it merely about words and speeches?"
"Music, music!
Is it merely about bells and drums?"
Draw this backward,
and one should also say:
"Mourning, mourning!
Is it merely about clothing?"
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ 孔子 established the Way of a new king,
clarifying that valuing intention leads to harmony,
and demonstrating that a fondness for sincerity eliminates hypocrisy.
"It is because it inherited the failings of Zhōu,
therefore it is like this."
The principle of the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals) is:
to have the people follow the ruler,
and to have the ruler follow Heaven.
It says:
"Considering the hearts of the people and ministers,
there cannot be a day without a ruler,
(since) there cannot be a day without a ruler,
and yet (the heir) still calls himself 'son' for three years,
(this is) because the heart of the ruler has not yet been properly established,
is this not having the people follow the ruler!
The heart of a filial son
is not yet appropriate for three years.
(But) if he ascends the throne the year after the three years is over,
it is in accordance with the beginning and end of the cycle of Heaven,
is this not having the ruler follow Heaven!
Therefore, to subdue the people and exalt the ruler,
(and) to subdue the ruler and exalt Heaven,
is the great meaning of the *Chūnqiū*.
The *Chūnqiū* discusses the affairs of twelve generations,
the Way of Man is fully understood and the Way of the King is complete.
The principles are spread throughout the two hundred and forty-two years,
assisting each other as left and right,
in order to create elegance,
their arrangement is interspersed,
It is not merely imitating the ancients.
Therefore, those who discuss the *Spring and Autumn Annals*
should combine and understand it thoroughly,
trace its origins and seek its meaning,
compare its similar instances,
match its categories,
examine its underlying principles,
and remove its redundancies.
Thus, the way of humanity is pervasive and the laws of the king are established.
Do you think this is not the case?
Now, the Son of Heaven ascends the throne after a year,
and the feudal lords within their fiefs call themselves "son" for three years;
these are not in the *Classic*,
but the way they are handled is no different than if they were in the *Classic*.
It is not that there is no distinction;
there is something seen, and the *Classic* can accept those additions.
Therefore, those who can use comparison to connect categories and use distinction to handle redundancies
have greatly understood it.
People receive their mandate from Heaven,
and have the nature of loving good and hating evil.
It can be nurtured but not changed,
can be predicted but not removed,
like the physical body which can become fat or thin,
but cannot be transformed.
Therefore, even if there is supreme virtue,
one can, for the sake of the ruler and parent, tolerate their evil,
but one cannot, for the sake of the ruler and parent, cause them to have no evil.
The *Book* says:
"When the sovereign does not act as a sovereign,
he loses his reverence."
Serving one's parents is also like this;
both are the extremes of loyalty and filial piety.
How could anyone but the most virtuous be like this?
If the father does not act as a father, then the son will not act as a son;
if the ruler does not act as a ruler, then the minister will not act as a minister.
Duke Wén was unable to observe mourning,
did not offer sacrifices at the proper times,
reversed the order by not observing the three-year mourning period,
and even married during mourning,
marrying a woman from a *dàfū* family,
thereby debasing the ancestral temple,
throwing his ancestral lines into confusion,
and rebelling against his predecessors.
He had not a single small good quality,
but four or five great evils;
therefore, the feudal lords did not give him their allegiance,
and the *dàfū* would not serve him.
These are signs of being detested and the effects of not being a minister.
He was insulted abroad
and plundered within;
he was a ruler without authority.
Confucius said:
"The administration has fallen into the hands of the *dàfū* for four generations now."
He was probably referring to the time since Duke Wén.
The gentleman knows that those in positions of authority cannot subdue people through evil.
Therefore, he selects the Six Arts to cultivate and nourish them.
The *Book of Poetry* and the *Book of Documents* express their aspirations.
The *Book of Rites* and the *Book of Music* purify their beauty.
The *Book of Changes* and the *Spring and Autumn Annals* illuminate their knowledge.
All six disciplines are grand,
and each has its strength.
The *Book of Poetry* speaks of aspiration,
therefore it excels in substance;
the *Book of Rites* establishes propriety,
therefore it excels in refinement;
the *Book of Music* praises virtue,
therefore it excels in influence;
the *Book of Documents* records achievements,
therefore it excels in matters of fact;
the *Book of Changes* is rooted in heaven and earth,
therefore it excels in numbers;
the *Spring and Autumn Annals* rectifies right and wrong,
therefore it excels in governing people;
one can obtain their respective strengths,
but one cannot exhaustively enumerate their details.
Therefore, if a ruler focuses solely on the grand principles, his wisdom will be obscured;
if he is overly broad in his learning, his endeavors will become weary.
These two represent different errors but lead to the same condemnation,
and the harm they cause will inevitably occur;
one must not fail to examine them.
Therefore, a good teacher
Since (one) admires its Dao,
one should be cautious in its practice.
Regulate the timing of early and late (activities),
bear the amount of much and little,
accommodate fast and slow (pace),
achieve without rushing,
examine without distress,
reflect on what one does,
and complete what one is absorbed in.
Therefore, strength is not taxed,
and the person is greatly accomplished.
This is called sage transformation;
I take it as my model.
Is the excellence of the *Spring and Autumn Annals* subtle?
It values the intent.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* cultivates the meaning of beginning and end,
comprehends the response to change and contingency,
penetrates the intention regarding life and death,
and fulfills the ultimate of human virtue.
Therefore, if the ruler is killed and the thief is punished,
then it is good to record their execution;
if no one punishes them,
then the ruler's burial is not recorded,
and the thief is not seen again.
Not recording the burial
is to indicate that there are no subjects and sons;
the thief not being seen again
Because it was fitting that it should be extinguished and cut off.
Now Zhào Dùn assassinated the ruler,
and four years later,
a separate entry was again recorded,
which is not the usual language of the *Spring and Autumn Annals*.
Scholars, past and present, differ and ask about it,
saying:
"This is an assassination of the ruler,
why is it recorded again?"
"It is like saying the rebels have not been punished,
why is a funeral recorded?
The reason a funeral is recorded,
is because it was not fitting to record a funeral, yet a funeral was recorded;
the reason it is recorded again,
is because it was not fitting to record it again, yet it was recorded again;
the two are connected by the same principle,
and cannot but be similar.
That Dùn was recorded again,
was simply to address the question and defend himself that he did not personally commit the assassination,
but it does not mean he should not be punished;
then one also cannot but say that the recording of Dào Gōng's funeral,
was simply to address the question and defend that the assassination was not completed,
and should not be blamed either.
If this is so, then the interpretation of the *Spring and Autumn Annals* is chaotic,
how can it be a model?"
"Therefore, to connect and compare in order to discuss right and wrong,
although it is difficult to fully grasp,
the principle is the same.
Now, to execute Dùn without precedent,
or not to execute without precedent,
